items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The pianist was a New Yorker named David Martin... Dave accompanied quite a few classical musicians... We recorded four numbers

ctx.x: We went into Florence for a short stay because Willie was engaged to play at a pavillion for the great Paris fair of 1937.

In October I recorded with Alix Combelle whom I spoke of before as being one of the first French jazz musicians that I became acquainted in 1935. The pianist was a New Yorker named David Martin who's family had a music school on 136th Street between 7th Avenue and Lenox. Dave

accompanied quite a few classical musicians and singers and was in Europe at this time accompanying Eddie South who was known as the "Dark Angel of the violin". Dave was also known as a jazz pianist and that was the reason he was on this date which was recorded under the name of Combelle. Wilson Meyers was on bass, Roger Chaput guitar and Jerry Mengo drums. We recorded four numbers of which "Hang Over Blues" was my composition.
